title: The Atlas contradicts itself on whether the Demand Absorption Buffer is part of Actively Stabilizing Collateral
content:
A.3.3.1.1 defines Actively Stabilizing Collateral as "highly liquid market making **non-USDS** assets," and A.3.3.1.2 defines the Demand Absorption Buffer as "highly liquid market making **USDS** assets." On that reading the two categories are disjoint by construction, which is the whole point — one is ammunition for buying USDS, the other is inventory for selling it.

A.3.3.2.3.1, in the implementation Section, says the opposite: Prime Agents must maintain a Demand Absorption Buffer, "**a subset of ASC** consisting of USDS that is for sale for at most 1.001 USD per USDS."

Both cannot hold. If DAB is a subset of ASC, then USDS counts toward ASC, contradicting the non-USDS definition; if ASC excludes USDS, then DAB cannot be a subset of it.

The difference is not cosmetic — it changes the required holdings. The DAB requirement is "25% of their required Actively Stabilizing Collateral" (A.3.3.2.3), i.e. 1.25% of the portfolio. Read as disjoint, an Agent must hold 5% in non-USDS ASC *plus* 1.25% in USDS, totalling 6.25%. Read as a subset, the 1.25% of USDS counts inside the 5%, and total reserves are 5% with only 3.75% available to buy USDS during a Peg Defense Event — a 25% reduction in the resource that defends the floor.

The ASC calculation lists (A.3.3.2.2.1.1.1 and A.3.3.2.2.1.2.1) favour the disjoint reading: every enumerated item is a Cash Stablecoin or USDC position, and the only USDS appearances are as the *pair* in a Curve or Uniswap pool, not as the counted asset. Meanwhile A.3.3.1.3.1 excludes USDS from the Agent Collateral Portfolio denominator entirely, which is hard to reconcile with USDS counting toward a ratio computed against it.

The subset language appears to be loose drafting, but it sits in the operative implementation Section rather than the conceptual one — and it is the Section an Agent would follow.
description: The conceptual framework defines ASC as non-USDS assets and DAB as USDS assets, making them disjoint; the implementation calls DAB 'a subset of ASC consisting of USDS.'
